must_fix.title: role="row" exception broken when the row is a shadow host: neither slotted nor shadow cells get hidden
must_fix.evidence:
acceptNode adds every hidden or rejected host to handledHosts and then rejects all of its children (`parent != null && handledHosts.has(parent)`) before the role=row exception, so a hidden row host's cells are never hidden. Before this change, with shadow DOM on, the native TreeWalker still hid the slotted cells, so this is a regression. Probe (yarn jest on a temporary test, flag enabled): body '
slotted

nits: With shadowDOM on, every walk(), including each MutationObserver-added subtree, runs querySelectorAllInShadowRoots, which does root.querySelectorAll('*') recursively. That is O(n) extra work per walk on large pages.
acceptNode now builds a new array with [...visibleNodes].some(...) for every visited node, even with the flag off. The old for..of loop avoided that allocation.
shadowRoots and pathNodes are computed once from the initial targets, so a shadow root that only holds an element later passed to keepVisible() is never observed.

report:
I'd hold the merge for one bug. In the shadow DOM path, a row that is itself a shadow host gets hidden, but its cells don't. Everything else checks out. **What passes** - `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`: 10 suites, 205 tests pass, including the new shadow DOM tests. - `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays` exits 0. - `yarn check-types` exits 0. - The other shadow DOM and overlay suites also pass: `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/focus packages/@react-aria/interactions packages/@react-aria/utils packages/react-aria-components/test/{Popover,Modal,ComboBox}` gives 23 suites, 374 passed and 2 skipped. - With shadow DOM support off, nothing changes: `createShadowTreeWalker` falls back to the native tree walker, and the new sets stay empty. - The new `@react-stately/flags` dependency (`^3.1.2`) matches the other packages that use it, and `yarn.lock` is updated to match. - The tests sit next to the existing `ariaHideOutside` tests and cover all five points in the issue. **Must fix: the `role="row"` exception breaks when the row is a shadow host** `ariaHideOutside` has a deliberate exception for rows. Because VoiceOver on iOS ignores `aria-hidden` on a `role="row"` element (WebKit bug 222623), the cells inside a hidden row are hidden as well. The new `handledHosts` check in `acceptNode` breaks this. It rejects every child of a host that was hidden, both its light DOM children and its shadow root children, before the row exception is checked. So when a hidden row is a shadow host, none of its cells get hidden, slotted or not. This is also a regression with shadow DOM support on. Before this change, the native tree walker still went into a hidden row's light children and hid the slotted cells. I reproduced it with a temporary test, which I deleted afterwards: ``` document.body.innerHTML = '
slotted
'; r.attachShadow({mode:'open'}).innerHTML = '
shadow cell
'; ariaHideOutside([t]); ``` The output: ``` light row cell hidden: true row hidden: true slotted cell hidden: null shadow cell hidden: null ``` `git status` ends exactly as I found it. ```json {"mergeable": false, "must_fix": [{"title": "role=\"row\" exception broken when the row is a shadow host: neither slotted nor shadow cells get hidden", "kind": "bug", "evidence": "acceptNode adds every hidden or rejected host to handledHosts and then rejects all of its children (`parent != null && handledHosts.has(parent)`) before the role=row exception, so a hidden row host's cells are never hidden. Before this change, with shadow DOM on, the native TreeWalker still hid the slotted cells, so this is a regression. Probe (yarn jest on a temporary test, flag enabled): body '
slotted
